transcripts.text: I haven't toured since, like, 2020, so it's been really, really fire to, like, get back out there on my own and touch the fans and be able to, like, give people an experience and also see that there are still so many people that love me. My community and my fan base is just growing. It's a beautiful thing. I'm extremely blessed. I'ma at this rate, I'ma at this rate, I'ma have to up the race, want stars in the race, belong in the gate, I need closure in space. Vulnerability is more of a super power. I feel like it has a bad stigma around it, like, oh, if you're vulnerable that means you're weak, or like you're leaving something open to be attacked or something, but I feel like true power and true connection starts with vulnerability. Any song you love so much and you feel so deeply connected to, It's because that person, that artist went through something and they, you know, were vulnerable enough to share it with you. Vulnerability is the birthplace of love. I thought it would be cool to try and inspire that.

I feel like I've always been a performer all of my life. I look at myself as a performer first before anything. So for me, it's extremely important, but for any artist, it's important in general to be one of your biggest streams of revenue. Once I did start making music, it kind of became second nature to me. My dad and my sister was in music when I was young, so I kind of just grew up heavily around music, and I don't see myself doing anything else. The growth is kind of crazy. I feel like my first project, I was just really just having fun. And I'm still having fun now, but I was really, really just having fun. Then I wasn't necessarily focused on being conceptual. Now, the evolution, the growth from my first project, which would have been 2060 from SoundCloud to now, which is Young Hard and Ronable, is like massive, massive growth. Like, I feel like me then, I was really just a baby. Like, I was just writing, you know, just writing anything, just coming up with melodies and hooks and stuff. But now, I am such a personal writer. Everything is me. It's almost like sometimes I don't know how to step outside of myself and write things that don't fully connect with me. So now, my music is a lot more sexy now versus my music then. It was a lot more just turn up and ah-ah-ah. I definitely think the growth is insane. I'm so blessed

Probably like four or five times I've done South by Southwest. I played the Color Agent stage and it was actually super dope. Honestly felt like a community, like it's a vibe. Everything that the Color Agent is doing is based around community. Doing a show and, you know, working with the team, that's what it's going to feel like. I feel like it's super important to have a platform that is based around community so that you can network more with people that do the same thing as you, but you might not even, you might not be able to come across them. but if you have somewhere where all these like-minded people are going to this one place to connect and to build, only beautiful things can come from that. If you're independent, if you're anything like me, then investing in yourself is non-stop. That's 24-7. You have to invest in yourself emotionally and spiritually, physically too, get in the gym. I think it's important. Before you invest in anything else other than the creator, you have to invest in you. I'm focused so right now in my life in staying where my feet are. I tend to trick myself out of my position when I think too far into the future. So, of course, I have goals and things that I want to accomplish. I want to come back around next year and do Dallas again, but even bigger. Really, really build up my foundation when it comes to touring. I have a lot of aspirations and goals when it comes to stuff like that. What's up? It's Cody Shane, magician, maverick, muse, and saint. And I'm TCA2. Let's go!
